styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small prop of about one tile. It has 12 visible tones per 16x16 tile, above tree-1a786c (7) and below tree-d43edd (29). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. Only 3% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline leans visibly cool grey or green-brown, matching the adjacent stone and moss rather than a black sticker line. The stones have about 4-5 lightness steps with a lit top edge and speckled grain. The moss is a clump of 2-3 greens on the upper surfaces, with a few dots trailing down the sides. It is simpler than the rich tree-d43edd canopy, and the stones could use more per-stone shading variety. It is at least as rich as the lower reference and reads as a craft-level piece rather than a flat sticker, so an artist would accept it beside the references.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small grey rock pile with a moss cap. Its measured facts are 12 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat coverage and 3% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted and not a black sticker line. It beats tree-1a786c (7 tones) on tone count but falls well short of tree-d43edd (29 tones). By eye, the stones show about 3-4 lightness steps (highlight, light grey, mid, dark) with a few speckle dots, and the moss has 2-3 greens. Beodeul uses 5-6 steps per material and shades each stone separately with per-clump highlights. Here the two or three rocks read as smooth lumps with little individual stone shading, and the moss is a small patch with little clumping. The piece is small and simple, so it is not failed for size, but its shading depth and texture are a little below the references. It is plausible but not clearly at the Beodeul bar, and when in doubt it fails.
